title: APC says let there be light, with raft of standards to speed up photonics manufacturing
gist: The Advanced Photonics Coalition released five standards covering co-packaged optics, silicon photonics test and manufacturing, and multicore fiber, aimed at enabling high-volume, multi-sourced photonics manufacturing. The release comes as Lumentum says its optical components are sold out through 2029 and as China-linked indium phosphide supply adds risk. Resolight CEO Ofer Shapiro argues that nanosecond optical circuit switching could reduce the number of transceivers needed.

insights.claim: Lumentum told Bloomberg its optical components are completely sold out through 2029 and it cannot meet demand for some products before 2028.
insights.so_what: Optical components are severely supply-constrained, giving suppliers like Lumentum strong pricing power.
insights.locator: But the photonics industry is struggling
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: Lumentum makes indium phosphide components critical for photonics, and China's position as a major indium phosphide producer adds geopolitical stress to the optical supply chain.
insights.so_what: Indium phosphide is a geopolitical chokepoint for AI optical networking.
insights.locator: But the photonics industry is struggling
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: Statements like Lumentum's raise fears that optical networking components are heading toward the shortages and price surges already hitting high-end DRAM and flash storage.
insights.so_what: Optical components could follow memory into a shortage-driven pricing cycle.
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: As AI hits the copper wall, rising data rates shorten copper's reach while raising heat and energy use, so datacenter operators are counting on optics to feed GPUs more data more efficiently.
insights.so_what: Structural demand for optical interconnect in AI datacenters.
insights.locator: The announcement, at the PECC Summit
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: The Advanced Photonics Coalition approved five standards at the PECC Summit: a CPO system architecture overview, CPO recommended practices, silicon photonics CPO test practices, a 4-core multicore fiber cable and connector specification, and a silicon photonics manufacturing specification.
insights.so_what: Common standards can speed CPO manufacturing scale-up and widen the supplier base.
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: The APC says common manufacturing, interface and test practices will remove implementation variations that add no market value and break supply chain silos that limit volume, enabling multiple sourcing.
insights.so_what: Multi-sourcing would ease shortages and pressure prices for optical components.
insights.quote: remove implementation variations that add no market value and overcome supply chain silos that constrain volume
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: The APC warns that without open standards the market will drift toward vertically integrated proprietary CPO solutions, fragmenting the market, increasing customer lock-in and slowing adoption.
insights.so_what: Open vs proprietary CPO is a key competitive battleground (e.g., versus Nvidia's integrated approach).
insights.quote: the natural gravitational pull is toward vertically integrated proprietary solutions
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: McKinsey advised AI operators to deploy optics-integrated CPO switches for higher bandwidth density and lower power per bit as AI shifts toward inference, and said a specialized architecture only earns its cost at volume.
insights.so_what: Inference growth supports CPO switch adoption.
insights.locator: Earlier this month, McKinsey flagged networking
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang demonstrated Spectrum X co-packaged optics technology at GTC, and Nvidia is among Lumentum's backers.
insights.so_what: Nvidia is pushing CPO and has ties to key optical component supply.
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: Resolight CEO Ofer Shapiro says scale-up networks currently co-deploy slow-switching OCS for reconfiguration and electronic data switches that are 1,000 times faster, and Resolight's nanosecond OCS aims to bring optical switching into the data plane.
insights.so_what: Fast OCS could displace some electronic data switching in AI scale-up.
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: Resolight says native photon routing, which keeps payloads in the light domain and avoids repeated optical-electrical-optical conversions, could greatly improve network energy efficiency and sharply reduce the number of transceivers needed in multi-rack AI scale-up networks.
insights.so_what: If adopted, fewer transceivers would be needed per AI cluster, a risk for transceiver volume forecasts.
insights.locator: By reducing repeated optical to electrical
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: Ofer Shapiro argues the answer to indium phosphide supply worries is to need less of it, by eliminating transceivers, rather than to find more supply.
insights.so_what: Architecture changes may ease optical supply constraints in place of capacity expansion.
insights.quote: The easiest to source and the greenest transceiver is the one that you don't need
insights.locator: “The easiest to source and the greenest
insights.speaker: Joe Fay

insights.claim: Digital Realty CTO Chris Sharp told the BBC that the industry is at the end of copper, as networking increasingly limits compute.
insights.so_what: Datacenter operators view optics as the next required network upgrade.
insights.quote: I think we're at the end of copper
insights.speaker: Joe Fay
